title: Cycling Speed Calculator: Average Speed and Pace
description: Convert ride distance and time into average cycling speed with the Cycling Speed Calculator — km/h, mph and pace per mile or kilometre. Free.
summary_sentence: For example, 42 km in 1 hour 54 minutes is an average of 22.1 km/h — a pace of about 2 minutes 43 seconds per kilometre.
quick_answer: The Cycling Speed Calculator converts a ride's distance and elapsed time into average speed and pace. Enter the distance you rode and the time it took, and read km/h and mph with the per-kilometre and per-mile splits — the numbers logs, group rides and 'was I faster?' are made of.

popular_table.title: Pace to speed
popular_table.intro: The same effort in the two dialects cyclists use — speed = 60 ÷ pace, computed.
popular_table.note: Averages hide stops: a moving average and an elapsed average are different truths, and this tool computes from the time you enter — enter elapsed for honesty, moving for flattery.

faq: Does this replace a specialist tool or professional measurement?
No — it is the arithmetic of average speed, exactly. Power, heart rate and GPS traces are richer instruments; this is the check they must agree with.
Is my input uploaded?
No. Distance and time are computed in your browser and stay there.
Does the route include live traffic?
No. Your time already includes the traffic you met; the calculator just divides.
Why is road distance longer than straight-line?
Roads wind. Enter the ridden distance — the one your wheels measured — or the average flatters you.
Can route results change over time?
Yours will, with fitness. The division does not change; the rider does.
Average speed or pace — which should I track?
Both describe the same ride; pace suits even-effort rides, speed suits comparing across distances. The table on this page converts between them.
Does it handle stops?
Only as you tell it: elapsed time includes them, moving time excludes them. Choose deliberately — the difference is the honest story of the ride.
My computer says a different average.
It may exclude auto-pauses, or include them, differently from the time you typed. Enter the same time definition the computer used before declaring a winner.
Pace per 5 km for time trials?
Multiply your per-km pace by 5 — or compute speed and divide the event distance by it. The calculator's splits scale linearly.
Downhill rides flatter the average?
Enormously, and the same arithmetic exposes it: compare like routes with like before celebrating a record.
